subject: Billing cadence & minimum commit — invoicing, taxes, net terms (Acme Analytics)
messages:
From: Maya Jenkins <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@acme-analytics.com (Tom Russell); finance@acme-analytics.com (PO Team)
Date: 2026-04-01T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Billing cadence & minimum commit — initial questions

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for sending over the Order Form draft. A few quick items from procurement/finance that we need clarity on before routing to our GPO: 

- Invoice cadence: can Redwood support quarterly invoices for committed spend, with monthly true-ups for overage? Our standard is quarterly billing for enterprise contracts.
- Minimum commit schedule: your Order Form lists an annual commit. Can we split the commit into two semi-annual buckets with a mid-year review?
- Net terms: are 60-day net acceptable for enterprise customers, or do you require 30?
- Taxes & withholding: will Redwood bill tax inclusive of local US state sales tax or will we be responsible for remitting?

I attached the Order Form Redwood sent (we re-saved it on our side). Please advise so we can keep the timeline for legal review this week.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Jenkins
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme Analytics
procurement@acme-analytics.com

Attachment: Redwood_OrderForm_v2.pdf
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Jenkins <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Billing cadence & minimum commit — initial questions

Hi Maya — great questions, thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and next steps below: 

- Invoice cadence: We can support quarterly invoices with monthly overage true-ups. We typically default to monthly billing but accept quarterly on enterprise deals.
- Minimum commit schedule: We prefer annual committed spend for predictability, but we can accept a two-period semi-annual split with a mid-year review and a small admin fee for restructuring (0.5% of committed value) — open to negotiation.
- Net terms: Standard is net 30 on hosted usage. Net 60 is something we can escalate to Sales Ops + Finance for this specific deal — need exec approval for the longer term.
- Taxes & withholding: Redwood bills net of taxes; we collect applicable sales/use taxes where required. For withholding, we need your country/state documentation to determine if withholding applies.

Next steps: I'm looping in our contracts/legal (hannah) and sales ops (marissa) to confirm what we can make standard vs. require approval. Hannah — can you review the attached redlines Maya will send and confirm if the semi-annual commit + net60 are acceptable with internal approvals? We will try to get a signed Order Form to DocuSign by next week if possible.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Date: 2026-04-03T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Billing cadence & minimum commit — internal review

Dylan / Marissa —

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed Maya's points against our standard Order Form and Redwood's billing policies. Notes below with proposed language to put into the redline (I'll produce a redlined PDF):

1) Invoice cadence: "Seller will invoice Customer quarterly in arrears for committed capacity. Seller will invoice monthly for any usage in excess of the committed amount; such overage invoices will be identified as 'Overage Charges' and will be due as set forth in the Payment Terms." (this preserves quarterly invoices but keeps overage clarity).

2) Minimum commit schedule: We can add a clause: "Customer's committed purchase shall be allocated to two (2) semi-annual performance periods for year one. A mid-year review will determine reallocation for the remainder of the year; any modifications are subject to Seller's written approval and may be subject to an administrative amendment fee not to exceed 0.5% of committed value." Please confirm the acceptability of 0.5% as a cap.

3) Net terms: If Acme requests net 60, we require finance approval. For deals requesting net >30, require approval flow: Account Exec -> Sales Ops -> Finance Director -> VP Revenue. We can include an approval block in the Order Form referencing that flow and note that extended terms are exceptions.

4) Taxes & withholding: Standard tax clause applies; we will collect applicable taxes. For cross-border withholding, we need completed W-8/W-9 or other relevant docs before any tax adjustments.

I'll attach the redline (Redlined_OrderForm_Acme.pdf) and call out the language. Marissa — can you confirm if sales is OK with the 0.5% admin cap? Dev — FYI if any billing system changes are needed to support quarterly invoices with monthly overage true-ups.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Billing cadence & minimum commit — redline review

Hi Hannah / Dylan,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the redline. A few follow-ups from Acme legal/finance after internal review: 

- The quarterly invoice + monthly overage approach is fine, but we need clarity on who owns the reconciliation in month +1 (Acme or Redwood) and an SLA for dispute windows (we propose 45 days from invoice date to raise disputes).
- The 0.5% admin cap is acceptable in principle but we would prefer language that any amendment fees be mutually agreed in good faith — can you tweak the clause to allow written confirmation in advance?
- Net 60: Acme requires net 60 for Enterprise Tier procurement. If Redwood needs approval, please route quickly. Without a confirmed net term, our finance team will not be able to issue the PO.
- Taxes: we will provide any necessary resale certificates/W-9 within five business days; please confirm Redwood's tax registration state so we can reconcile.

Can we target DocuSign circulation next Monday? If you can get Finance approval for net 60 before then, that would keep our timeline intact.

Regards,
Tom Russell
Senior Counsel | Acme Analytics
legal@acme-analytics.com

Subject: Re: Billing cadence & minimum commit — final steps & DocuSign

Tom / Maya —

Appreciate the clear items. Quick status update and asks: 

- Reconciliation & disputes: We will accept a 45-day dispute window and will mark reconciliation responsibility as "Seller provides invoice detail; Customer must raise disputes within 45 days; in the event of a bona fide dispute, parties will work in good faith to reconcile."
- Amendment fee language: Hannah updated the redline to require "mutual written consent" for any administrative amendment fee; see attached redline.
- Net terms: Sales Ops / Finance have approved net 60 for this deal (deal_id DL-8347) — I've received confirmation from our Finance Director. We will include exception approval language in the Order Form as standard practice.
- Taxes: Redwood is registered in California for sales tax collection; we will accept W-9 / resale cert and will apply taxes accordingly.

Next steps: I've attached the final redlined PDF and started the DocuSign envelope: https://app.docusign.com/ACME/Envelope/12345. Please review and confirm signatories so we can circulate. If all good, I'll pull in our Rev Ops director for signature on Redwood's side.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this week.

Best,
